title: Circular-launch models of small exposed graphite made before 2010 give too little infrared light for Gaia20cdd in 2014-2024
abstract: Can old exposed dust keep the infrared excess of Gaia20cdd for ten years? We combine the published 2010 W3 upper bound with radiation-pressure motion and grain cooling. For compact graphite of radius 0.05-0.30 um, a positive-light inequality limits all non-negative mixtures of the tested grain sizes and past release times. A numerical search over circular launch radii of 0.01-100 au and release ages up to 100 years gives W2 excesses below 0.006 in 2014 and 0.000024 in 2024, as fractions of stellar W2 light. The reported persistent excess is 0.248 +/- 0.080. The bound needs no dust mass, size power law, or W3 detection. Thus this exposed small-graphite model needs dust made after 2010. A steady outflow fit gives a source at 2.32 au for one K star or 3.40 au for a K+K binary, about 30 percent closer than a shell with the same grains. It needs 2.08 or 2.70 x 10^22 g of new small dust per year. After production stops, 90 percent of W2 light disappears in 0.61 or 0.73 years; W3 and W4 last longer. The 21 quiet NEOWISE visits fit continued production better than one release by score differences of 41 or 11, for assumed common colour errors of 0.03 or 0.06 mag. The mixture bound has an exact additive-light step and a numerical physical maximum. It is not a proof for all sizes or orbits. Shielding, gas, bound grains, another material, a second emitter or an incorrect photosphere can change the result. One impact can still make fragments that continue to produce dust. We preserve code, source hashes, model profiles and checks. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-ad674de38a9a; topic astronomy; machine hp; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: The 2010 W3 upper bound limits W2 light from any non-negative mixture of the tested old exposed graphite grains. The upper envelope is far below the reported persistent excess. This is a numerical result for circular launch radii of 0.01-100 au and release ages up to 100 years, without shielding or gas.
After a steady source stops, W2 fades on a shorter time scale than W3 and W4. The right panel shows a single dust release. These are predictions at the best outflow fits, not measured shutdowns.
A full motion and cooling model moves the best graphite source inward by about 30 percent compared with a shell using the same grains. W2 and W3 errors leave broad radius and rate ranges.
